destination.name: Mount Remarkable National Park
destination.tagline: A 960 m summit, rocky gorges and bike trails at the Flinders Ranges' southern end.
destination.description: Mount Remarkable National Park rises above the Willochra Plain at the southern end of the Flinders Ranges, 45 km north of Port Pirie. Walking tracks lead to a 960 m summit and through gorges cut into ancient rock, and valley trails are home to echidnas and lace monitors. The Willowie trails and the Remarkable Epic trail draw mountain bikers, and Melrose, the oldest town in the Flinders Ranges, sits at the foot of the mountain.

goodToKnow.title: Pay entry before you arrive
goodToKnow.detail: Vehicle entry is $14.40 and must be paid in advance, online or through a booking agent. Camping fees are also paid before arrival.

goodToKnow.title: Check closures first
goodToKnow.detail: Fire danger and pest-control programs close the park, and part of Alligator Gorge is shut after the 2025 Wilmington fire.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: {months} bring cool days that suit the summit hike and the gorge walks.

notes: Coordinates left null for the pin pass: use a visitor point (Mambray Creek camp/visitor area on the west side or the Alligator Gorge car park), not the park centroid and not Alligator Gorge's or the summit's pin; Melrose is the gateway town.
Span 55 km kept: Horrocks Pass (about 20 km from the park's middle) and Melrose are inside 75% (41 km).

Source of facts: parks.sa.gov.au Mount Remarkable page (960 m summit, Willochra Plain, Willowie trails, Remarkable Epic, fees, closures, 45 km north of Port Pirie), flindersandoutback.com.au Melrose page (oldest town in the Flinders Ranges).
